summary: Sliderock Mountain lookout, Granite County MT: a 40-ft L-4 tower by 1935, moved to Fort Missoula museum in 1983 or 1984; the mountain tower is gone.

facts.design: L-4 type, 40-foot pole tower (firelookout.com); museum describes an L-4 support structure
facts.status_note: The tower on Sliderock Mountain is listed as gone; the cab and part of the tower were moved to the Fort Missoula Historical Museum.

access.note: Stands on the grounds of the Fort Missoula Historical Museum. The museum page describes visitors standing on a landing between two flights of stairs; no hours or climbing rules were found.

events.note: Site first developed with a 35-foot pole platform and a scale-model log cabin.
Museum dates the lookout to about 1930; the marker says it was manufactured in Columbia Falls that year.
Firelookout.com says a 40-foot pole L-4 tower was built on the site.
Taken apart on its mountain and moved to the Fort Missoula museum, with help from the Friends of the Historical Museum and the Missoula Chapter of the Society of American Foresters.
Firelookout.com says the cab and top two-thirds of the tower went to Fort Missoula. Conflicts with the 1983 date.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Kemnow gives Lolo/Admin. Deer Lodge National Forest; firelookout.com gives Lolo National Forest alone. The story uses Kemnow's name and notes the other.
The museum and the marker say 1983; firelookout.com says 1984 and describes only the cab and top two-thirds moving. The sources are not reconciled, so the story reports both.
The museum and the marker date manufacture to 1930; firelookout.com dates the 40-foot L-4 tower on the site to 1935. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: A separate record, us-mt-sliderock-at-fort-missoula-historical-museum, already covers the structure at the museum; this story covers the original site and cross-links to it in spirit. No staffing or fire evidence turned up in the sources read or in one web search, so those sections are left out. firelookout.com's header reads 'R.I.P. 1928-1966' without explanation, and it does not match its own 1919 and 1935 dates; it was not used. Access at the museum is inferred from the museum page; check hours with the museum.
